items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe... [INTERVIEWEE] Thank you, Monk.

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have with me Mr. Jon Hendricks.
Thank you, Monk. That’s a great name.
It works. I’ll bet you’ve said that a few times.

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Monk told me that Miles begin to play Dizzy’s best notes... Monk was so beautiful, because he was a great teacher... Monk said the same thing. He said, 'Just do what you do...'

ctx.x: Was there a hierarchy of musicians there?

Yeah. It was Bird and Diz on the bebop scene. Miles was kind of a crown prince. He was still in his Dizzy mode. It was Monk that told Miles, you better stop playing like Dizzy and get your own stuff, because Miles was playing like Dizzy, in that he began to – so Monk told me that Miles begin to play Dizzy’s best notes. I said, wow. Then I thought of – I was doing the words to Round Midnight, and I was doing the Miles version [Hendricks sings the introduction to that version]. Then I remembered Dizzy’s version was…
Let’s go there for a moment. So Monk played other instruments as well.
